text:
Maya (customer): Hi team — after our IdP certificate rotation yesterday a bunch of users see 'SAML response: Recipient/AssertionConsumerServiceURL mismatch'. We rolled the cert at 02:10 UTC. No config changes on our side other than the key rollover. Login worked before. Help?

Alex (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the IdP metadata XML or a link? Also what exact ACS URL are you sending in the AuthnRequest?

Maya (customer): Link to metadata: https://idp.example.com/metadata.xml (public for now). Our app ACS is https://app.customer.com/sso/acs (we recently changed from /auth/saml/acs). We saw a spike of 502 -> but primary error in our logs is the mismatch message from your SP.

Alex (support): Got it. Two quick checks while we dig in: 1) confirm the exact ACS in the SP config on Redwood side (trailing slash matters), 2) can you grab the raw SAML response we receive (base64)? If you prefer, I can enable debug logging for this connection and share sanitized output.

Maya (customer): Pasted the raw response here (sanitized):
```
<samlp:Response Destination="https://app.customer.com/sso/acs" ...>
  <saml:Assertion>
    <saml:Subject>
      <saml:SubjectConfirmation>
        <saml:SubjectConfirmationData Recipient="https://app.customer.com/auth/saml/acs" .../>
      </saml:SubjectConfirmation>
    </saml:Subject>
  </saml:Assertion>
</samlp:Response>
```
Maya (customer): Notice Recipient is the old path /auth/saml/acs. We think our SP library is still building the AuthnRequest with the old ACS; we rotated certs then flipped a feature flag for new ACS a few hours later.

Alex (support): That explains the mismatch — the response recipient must match the SP-configured ACS exactly. Two followups: did the IdP metadata include both ACS endpoints or only the new one? And did the IdP sign the response with the new cert or the old cert?

Maya (customer): IdP metadata has one <AssertionConsumerService> location="https://app.customer.com/sso/acs" index="0"/>, so only the new. The signature is with the new cert (thumbprint SHA1: AB:12:34:CD:...). But the SubjectConfirmationData shows the old recipient because our app read an old cached SP config from our CDN edge.

sre-bot: support-debug-logging enabled for maya-corp.com connection (trace id: rwd-ff12ab).

Jordan (eng-oncall): Quick note from the runtime side: our SP verification step enforces Recipient equality (we treat trailing slash and exact path as part of the check). We do not currently accept multiple recipients in the same response. Workaround: if the IdP will include both ACS locations in metadata or the response uses the metadata-declared ACS endpoint, it'll pass. Short-term we can relax the strictness per-tenant but that needs a cross-team change (security review).

Sam (security): Re relaxing validation: not ideal. Accepting multiple recipients or doing a looser equality makes replay/redirect attack surface larger. Prefer these approaches in order: 1) have the customer ensure the AuthnRequest & cached SP configs align with the metadata (recommended), 2) IdP to set the response Recipient to match the metadata-declared ACS, or 3) for emergency only, allow a per-tenant switch to accept a whitelist of previous ACS paths (audit logged).

Alex (support): For this customer I propose: 1) we enable debug logs (done), 2) Olivia from CS to coordinate a maintenance window so they can purge CDN edge cache and rotate SP config on their side to the new ACS, 3) if they can't, we can temporarily add their old path to an allowed-recipient list (expires automatically in 24h) — requires security ack. @Sam ok for the temp whitelist?

Olivia (customer-success): I'll coordinate with Maya. Maya — can you confirm how many users affected and if you can do a short cache purge? We can schedule a 30-min window.

Maya (customer): ~120 users failed during the morning spike. We can purge the CDN and flip the feature flag right away; need help confirming Redwood will accept the new ACS after purge.

Sam (security): Temporary whitelist OK for 24h for incident remediation only. Must log all attempts and notify if any stale cert signatures are used. Alex — please enable whitelist for tenant maya-corp with audit tag "temp-whitelist-4780012345" and set TTL 24h.

Alex (support): Done — added allowed-recipient entry for tenant maya-corp for recipient https://app.customer.com/auth/saml/acs (ttl=24h). Debug logs show subsequent response now accepted when we replay the sample. Please purge CDN and flip the flag; I'll watch the trace. :eyes: 

Maya (customer): Purged CDN edges + flipped flag. Re-tested sign-in flow for one user, successful. Thank you! :tada:

Alex (support): Great. Next steps: 1) Maya to confirm broader rollout in 2 hours, 2) Maya to confirm IdP metadata contains the correct cert thumbprint (we saw new cert in metadata), 3) Sam to review and remove whitelist after TTL or earlier after rollback confirmation, 4) Jordan to file a small SP enhancement to make debug logs more explicit about recipient mismatch (internal ticket rwd-issue-8912).

Jordan (eng-oncall): Filed rwd-issue-8912 to add clearer mismatch diagnostics (will include expected vs received recipient and index from metadata).

Sam (security): I'll monitor the tenant's audit logs and remove whitelist earlier if everything looks clean.

Olivia (customer-success): Maya — please post back in this thread once you've validated with full user base so we can close.

Maya (customer): Will do. Appreciate the quick help, team.

sre-bot: incident-note: temporary-whitelist-4780012345 created by Alex, TTL=24h.

Alex (support): Closing loop: whitelist removed at TTL expiry with no further failures observed. Marking resolved unless Maya reports otherwise. :white_check_mark:
